title: JamBench observatory weekly log - Nov 30 2026
body:
JamBench observatory weekly sync — condensed notes

Date: 2026-11-30
Attendees: Emily Chen (owner), Raj Patel, Sofia Alvarez, Liam O'Neill, Priya Rao, Ashwin K. (SRE drop-in)
Duration: 45 minutes
Location: Zoom + perf-observatory channel

Goal: capture oddball throughput/latency signatures from last week's JamBench sampling, triage hypotheses, and assign follow-ups for targeted lab runs. This session focused on a new wildcard sampling artifact we observed on 11/27 that produced repeatable p95 jitter under mixed-short workloads.

1) TL;DR of discoveries
- New wildcard sample pattern: short-hot bursts (~30–90s) that reduce effective QPS by ~25% on a 4k context model variant when prefix-cache miss-rate spikes above 18%.
- Worst-impacted quantiles: p95 increased from 68ms -> 140ms; p99 tails show step-like jumps to ~420ms during burst window. p50 relatively stable.
- Reproducer: JamBench run id JB-20261127-wild-4 produced the signature on two different clusters (g4x2 and private-dedicated pool).
- Correlated signal: KV cache churn and small-batch kernel fallback events observed in runtime logs at the same timestamps.

2) Data & quick metrics (summarized)
- Baseline steady-state: 950 QPS sustained, p50=42ms, p95=68ms, p99=120ms.
- JamBench wildcard window: 720 QPS effective (control client issued same load), p50=45ms, p95=140ms, p99=420ms. CPU/GPU util: GPU memory pressure up by 8% during window, CPU-side scheduler loops increased 2x.
- KV cache stats: miss-rate jumped from 5% -> 18% concurrent with bursts; median KV latency jumped 1.8x.

3) Repro attempts and environment notes
- Repro on mainline (docker image: serving-runtime:2026-11-25) succeeded on two independent clusters. Repro runs used JamBench config: mixed-short-heavy.json (seq_len distribution 16/64/512).
- Repro without prefix caching disabled: no burst signature observed, which strengthens cache-churn hypothesis.
- Shadow run with disabled micro-batching heuristic (experimental flag --heuristic-v2=false) reduced p95 increase by ~40% but worsened throughput consistency; implies interaction between batching heuristics and cache state.

4) Hypotheses (ranked)
H1 (primary): prefix/KV cache temperature sweep causes more frequent cold hits; the runtime shifts to a slower kernel path for affected sequences causing latency tailing.
H2: batching heuristic oscillation under mixed sequence lengths leads to microbatch fragmentation and kernel fallback (esp. for quantized kernels) causing increased completion time for some requests.
H3: rare scheduler starvation from background maintenance tasks (checkpointing / eviction) aligns with burst windows. Lower confidence; observed in one cluster trace.

5) Quick instrumentation gaps to fill
- Need finer-grained KV cache telemetry per-pod: sample-size, eviction-rate per-second, origin sequence id tag.
- Add histogram of kernel selection frequency (fast/slow quant paths) keyed by sequence-length bucket.
- Correlate JamBench client-side timing (enqueue->ack) with pod-level L1/L2 cache miss counters if available.

6) Immediate actions and owners (short horizon, 1–7 days)
- Emily: schedule targeted JamBench sweep JB-20261201-ext to run 20 iterations across 3 clusters with explicit cache seeding/eviction toggles. (Due: 2026-12-01)
- Raj: add a short patch to runtime to emit kernel-selection events as lightweight logs (flag: --emit-kernel-events) and land PR. JIRA-RT-2127. (Due: 2026-12-02)
- Sofia: add per-pod KV cache eviction rate metric to Prometheus exporter and create dashboard panel in Console under serving-runtime/observatory. (Due: 2026-12-03)
- Liam: reproduce experiment with microbatching disabled/enabled and record end-to-end traces; store traces in S3 perf-buckets/jb-repros/. (Due: 2026-12-02)
- Priya: run a maintenance-task blackout window (disable eviction scripts) during one JamBench sweep to test H3. (Due: 2026-12-04)

7) Longer-term work (2–6 weeks)
- Engineering spike (owner: Raj): evaluate a TTL-backed KV cache policy vs current LRU to reduce temperature storms; prototype in a branch and run A/B tests against JamBench. (Estimate: 3 weeks)
- Product/Console (owner: Sofia): add a per-route 'cache-heat' warning that surfaces when miss-rate exceeds threshold for >60s to help SREs route traffic or increase cache allocations. (Estimate: 2 weeks)
- Perf team: expand JamBench sample space to include synthetic 'prefix-churn' traces that intentionally rotate a small set of prefixes at high QPS to exercise cache eviction boundaries.

8) Risks and mitigations discussed
- Risk: naive mitigation (increase cache sizes) could mask other issues (batching scheduling) and increase cost; prefer targeted experiments first.
- Mitigation: run canary changes on dedicated pool with controlled traffic; use fallback policy to hosted variants if regressions exceed thresholds.

9) Notes on cross-team coordination
- SRE may need to temporarily provision an extra dedicated pool for long-running JamBench sweeps to avoid impacting prod shadow runs. (Ashwin to confirm capacity)
- Solutions Eng: keep a short customer-facing note ready if we detect customer-affecting regressions; target hold until we have root cause and mitigation.

10) Open questions for next sync
- Is kernel fallback strictly tied to quantized model variants? (obs: stronger signature on 4-bit variants in JB runs)
- What is the threshold cache-miss-rate that reliably predicts burst onset? (need ROC-style analysis)

Appendix: quick reproducible commands
- Run reproducer (local): ./tools/jambench --config=experiments/mixed-short-heavy.json --iterations=20 --id=JB-20261201-ext
- Enable kernel logs: export SR_RUNTIME_FLAGS=\"--emit-kernel-events\" and restart pod set perf-lab-1

Next sync: Wednesday 2026-12-02 (15:00 PST) — focus on results from JB-20261201-ext and first kernel-events PR landing.

End of notes.
